Luke 9.27.</ns0:note> AND he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, that there be some of them that stand here, which shall not tast of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.<ns0:note place="bottom">To <ns0:hi>tast of Death,</ns0:hi> is the same with <ns0:hi>to Dye,</ns0:hi> or to begin to Dye, or to <ns0:hi>exprience Death</ns0:hi>: compare with this Text, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 34 8. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 14.24. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 8.52. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.9. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.4.5. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.3. <ns0:hi>till they have seen the Kingdom of God come.</ns0:hi> Our Evangelist addeth <ns0:hi>with Power.</ns0:hi> It cannot be meant of the <ns0:hi>day of Iudgment,</ns0:hi> unless in the type of it, which was in the <ns0:hi>destruction of Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> (of which many understand it) for some of the <ns0:hi>Ap<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>stles,</ns0:hi> more doubtless of Christs Disciples, outlived the fatal ruin of that once Famous City. Others understand here by the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of God, Christs Resurrection from the Dead,</ns0:hi> when Christs Kingdom began to be fully made known, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.42.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 And after six days, Jesus taketh with him, Peter,<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> and James, and John, and leadeth them up into <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>n high mountain apart by themselves, and he was transfigured before them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And there appeared unto them Elias, with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master it is good for us to be here, and let us make three taber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 For he wist not what to say, for they were sore afraid.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:285" />7 And there was a cloud that overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son, hear him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And suddenly, when they had looked round a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another, what the rising from the dead should mean.<ns0:note place="bottom">Both <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> as well as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> bear record to the Truth of this History. See the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth. Ch.</ns0:hi> 17.1. Our Saviour was pleased thus to fortify these three of his Disciples against his Passion, which they were soon to see. And also to confirm their Faith as to his <ns0:hi>Divine Nature</ns0:hi>; why <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> rather then any others appeared, is but a curious question of no great use to us, if resolved, and not possible to be resolved. These three Disciples, by this Apparition saw our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour owned by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> who gave the Law, and by <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> in great repute both of them with the Jews. The three Disciples could know neither of them (dead many hundreds of years before they were in being) but by <ns0:hi>Revelation:</ns0:hi> probably Christ told them who they were, what their Discourse with Christ was in the ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral, <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> telleth us. There is no considerable thing in this <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> Relation, which we did not meet with in <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> which may supersede any further Labo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r about it here,</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 17.10</ns0:note> that Elias must first come?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And he answered, and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 22.6 Isa. 53.2<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny things, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Phil. 2.7.</ns0:note> be set at nought.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But I say unto you, that Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.<ns0:note place="bottom">Christ had been telling his Disciples that he should <ns0:hi>suffer.</ns0:hi> The Jews had a <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> not only that the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> should come, but that <ns0:hi>he should be cut off, Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.26. but <ns0:hi>not for himself.</ns0:hi> Only this hindred, the certainty of their persuasion, that Christ was he, because <ns0:hi>Elias was not yet come,</ns0:hi> whom they did expect, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.5. for they expected the coming of <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> in Person, when as the Prophecy was to be understood of one <ns0:hi>in the Spirit, and Power of</ns0:hi> Elias, as the Angel expounded it, <ns0:hi>Lu.</ns0:hi> 1.17. They also expected that <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> when he came, should make a great change in their World, and bring all things again into order, but still their Eye was upon a <ns0:hi>secular Change,</ns0:hi> and a restoring of them to that <ns0:hi>Liberty</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Country,</ns0:hi> which they formerly enjoyed, where as the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.6. is expounded by the <ns0:hi>Angel, Lu.</ns0:hi> 1.16, 17. <ns0:hi>And many of the Children of</ns0:hi> Israel <ns0:hi>shall he turn to the Lord their God—to turn the Hearts of the Fathers un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the Children, and the disobedient to the Wisdom of the just, to make ready a People prepared for the Lord.</ns0:hi> The Disciples being <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> were under the prejudices of these Notions about <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> so commonly received by the <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Church,</ns0:hi> and the Generality of their People. To this our Saviour Answers, The thing was true, <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> (that is one <ns0:hi>in the Spirit and Power of Elias</ns0:hi>) was according to the <ns0:hi>Prophecy</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Malachy</ns0:hi> to come, before the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> but they had over-lookt him, for indeed this <ns0:hi>E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ias</ns0:hi> was come, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.14. and by his Preaching the Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine of <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Remission of Sins,</ns0:hi> had indeavou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red to <ns0:hi>restore</ns0:hi> all things, that is, to make a great change in the Hearts, and lives of the Jews, but they had put him to death, he further telleth them, That <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> had told them of the Son of Man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought. He did indeed tell them so, when <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.29. he pointed to him passing by, and said, <ns0:hi>Behold</ns0:hi> the Lamb <ns0:hi>of God who taketh away</ns0:hi> [or taketh up, or beareth] <ns0:hi>the Sins of the World.</ns0:hi> So that this was no just prejudice to their believing, that he was the true <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And when he came to <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And straightway all the people, when they be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />held him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, saluted him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And he asked the scribes, What question ye <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>among your selves.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> with them.<ns0:note place="bottom">When Christ came down from the Mountain of <ns0:hi>Transfigura<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion,</ns0:hi> to his Disciples, which he had left at the Foot of the Moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain, he saw a great Multitude got together about them, and di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scerned some <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> (Companions of the Pharisees and Teachers of the Law) mixing themselves with his Disciples, and Arguing with them. They had often attempted our Saviour to no purpose, but their own shame and Confusion, in his absence they fall in with his Disciples, who were yet raw in the Faith, over them they hope to get a great Conquest. The Evangelist doth not plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly tell us what the subject matter of their Discourse was. Tho there be no question but the Scribes in this Discourse pursued their Design to expose, and vilify Christ, and his Disciples, and to that purpose taking advantage of our Saviours absence discoursed with them about many <ns0:hi>Things,</ns0:hi> yet Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> doth (not im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />probably) judge that a great part of their Discourse, was about our Saviours <ns0:hi>Casting out of Devils, and their Power in that thing derived from him,</ns0:hi> they being at the present non-plust, and not able to exert that Power in the casting out of a Devil, with which one was possessed, who in our Saviours Absence was brought to them. That which maketh this probable, is not only that this <ns0:hi>Act</ns0:hi> of our Saviour more troubled and Gall'd them than any other, and put them to that miserable <ns0:hi>Refuge,</ns0:hi> (out of which our Saviour had lately beaten them) to say, <ns0:hi>That he cast out Devils, by</ns0:hi> Beelzebub <ns0:hi>the Prince of Devils,</ns0:hi> but also that when our Saviour coming in to the timely Rescue of his Disciples, as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ke's the Scribes. What Question you <ns0:hi>among your selves,</ns0:hi> it is said.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> one of the multitude, answered, and said, Master! I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And wheresoever he taketh him, he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>dashe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> him.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> teareth him, and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away, and I spake to thy disciples, that they should cast him out, And they could not.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 He answered him, and saith, O faithless gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you?? bring him unto me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And they brought him unto him, And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.26.</ns0:note> when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him, and he fell on the ground, and wallowed, foaming.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And oft-times, it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters to destroy him, but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Jesus said unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 17.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> If thou canst believe, all things <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> possible to him that believeth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 And straightway the father of the child cryed out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe, help thou my unbelief.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, Come out of him, and enter no more into him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And <ns0:hi>the spirit</ns0:hi> cryed, and rent him sore, and came out of him, and he was as one dead, insomuch that many said, He is dead.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up, and he arose.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And when he was come into the house, his dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.<ns0:note place="bottom">This famous History is also recorded by two other Evangelists, <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> we have opened it in our Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 17.14, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and consider'd what <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> have to Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pleat it. For our Instruction we may learn several things from the Consideration of it. 1. The great goodness of God in pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serving us from the power of Evil Spirits, as also the daily work<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of his Providence for our preservation, what but this kept this Man from being destroyed by the Fires and the Waters into which he had been often thrown by the Evil Spirit. 2. That the shorter the Devils time is, the more he rageth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. This is true, both as to the Devil himself, and his Instruments, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 12.12. <ns0:hi>The Devil is come down unto you, having great Wrath, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he knoweth that he hath but a short time.</ns0:hi> Thus in the moment of Conversion, Christians often meet with the strongest Conflicts of Temptation. 3. The fault is not in Christ, but in our selves, if we receive not that Mercy from him, which he hath, and which we stand in need of, and beg from him.—If (saith Christ) <ns0:hi>thou canst believe.</ns0:hi>—4. God rewardeth weak Faith, where it is attended with a sincere desire of increase. This poor Man shewed a very imperfect Faith, in saying, <ns0:hi>If thou canst do any thing,</ns0:hi> but it being in some degree and sincere, the Lord rewardeth it, tho Weak, he desiring an increase of it, and that God would from his goodness supply what was defective in his Faith. 5. The great Cures both of our <ns0:hi>Bodies</ns0:hi> and Souls in some Cases, require more Extraordinary, and Importunate Addresses, and applications unto God, more especially where Evils are more inverate. For other things relating to this History, see the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 17. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee, and he would not that any man should know <ns0:hi>it.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:285" />31 For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him, and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour, as the time of his suffering approached more near<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, did more frequently inculcate it to his Disciples, that being forewarned, they might also be fore-armed against the <ns0:hi>Tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion</ns0:hi> of it, and we learn from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 24.21. That all was too lit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tle, for when they saw these things <ns0:hi>come to pass,</ns0:hi> they began to Flag as to their Faith. They said, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>But we trusted it had been he, who should have Redeemed</ns0:hi> Israel. Our Saviour, the <ns0:hi>Son of Man is delivered,</ns0:hi> which is expounded by <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> 17.22, 23. <ns0:hi>The Son of Man shall be betrayed.</ns0:hi> He was already de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />livered in the sure Counsel of God, and what God hath revealed, shall be done, because of the certainty of the effect, is often in Scripture spoken of as a thing already done, that Phrase, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. the <ns0:hi>third Day</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> expounds that other Phrase which we meet with, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.31. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which we Tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />slate <ns0:hi>after three Days,</ns0:hi> and makes the meaning of the Evangelist plain to have been, as we determined it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And he came to Capernaum, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.46.</ns0:note> and being in the house, he asked them What was it that ye di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sputed amongst your selves by the way?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 But they held their peace, For by the way they had disputed among themselves who <ns0:hi>should be</ns0:hi> the greatest.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Ambition of the Disciples we have had occasion before to Discourse of, in the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 18.1. It was founded up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on their mistake of the true Nature of the <ns0:hi>Kingdom</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siah,</ns0:hi> which they at this time, and a long time after (even to the time of Christs Ascension, as appeareth by <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.6.) under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood of a temporal, secular Kingdom, in the Administration of which, he should deliver the Jews from all Slavery, and Bondage, this made their Minds so often run of <ns0:hi>Dignities,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Places</ns0:hi> which he should in that Administration, have a Power to dispose of. This made the Mother of <ns0:hi>Zebedees</ns0:hi> Children, petition for pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces for her two Sons.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And he sate down and called the twelve, and saith unto them,<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.43. Luke 9.46.</ns0:note> If any man desire to be first the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.16.</ns0:note> he took a child, and set him in the midst of them, and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 10.40.</ns0:note> whosoever shall re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Matthews</ns0:hi> Recital of this passage, expoundeth <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi>; he saith, Christ said, <ns0:hi>except you be converted, and become as little Children, you shall not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, who<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever therefore shall humble himself as this little Child, the same is greatest in the Kingdom of God. And whoso shall receive one such little Child in my Name, receiveth me. Luke</ns0:hi> also relateth this passage something more shortly, but without any Contradiction to what is said by the other Evangelist. The Sence is plain our Saviours design was to Check the Ambition, and Ignorance of his Disciples. Never more unseasonably shewed then now, when a suffring time was so hard at Hand. He at first did it by Word of Mouth, telling them. <ns0:hi>That if any Man desire to be first, he should be last of all.</ns0:hi> The least valuable in the Eyes of God, and he would have them value such a Person least, <ns0:hi>Humility</ns0:hi> is that which most Exalts a Soul in the Eyes of Christ, and setteth it highest in his esteem. But it is observable. Our Lord doth not say. He that is the first, but he who <ns0:hi>desir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to be first.</ns0:hi> God is a God of order, not of Confusion, there can be no order without a first, as well as a last. But Christians (Ministers especially<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> for he is here speaking to the Twelve) ought to be sought out for, not to seek places of Preheminence, and Dignity, he that is <ns0:hi>first</ns0:hi> in seeking them, is usually <ns0:hi>last</ns0:hi> as to any true worth deserving them, and ought last to obtain them. Then he teacheth them <ns0:hi>Humility</ns0:hi> by the Type of a <ns0:hi>little Child,</ns0:hi> which he setteth in the midst of them, telling them they must be <ns0:hi>like that little Child</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi>) not in all things, but in the want of <ns0:hi>Ambition:</ns0:hi> in a carelessness as to the great things of this Life. And whosoever entertain'd or shewed kindness to such a one, Christ would take it as done to himself, and what kindness was shewed him, reached not to him only, but to his Father who sent him. There are also other things in little Children commen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded to us in Holy Writ, but this is manifestly what our Saviour here intendeth. See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.                <ns0:p n="38">38 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 9.49.</ns0:note> And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed not us, and we forbad him, because he follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed not us.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 But Jesus said, Forbid him not, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 12.3.</ns0:note> for there is no man that shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 12.30.</ns0:note> For he that is not against us, is on our part:<ns0:note place="bottom">Here is a question ariseth worthy of our Discussion a little, see<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing these Miraculous Operations were performed by a Divine Power, and for such an end as the Confirmation of Christs <ns0:hi>Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Power,</ns0:hi> how could any one cast out Devils in the Name of Christ, and yet not follow him, and his Disciples? 1. It is appa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rent, that this Person was no Enemy to Christ, or his Gospel, by what our Saviour saith, both <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39. and 40. 2. It is evident. <ns0:hi>That the casting out of Devils,</ns0:hi> was no saving effect of the holy Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit, Christ saith, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.22. That some should say, <ns0:hi>In thy Name have we cast out Devils,</ns0:hi> to whom in the Day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment he would say. <ns0:hi>Depart from me, I know you not, you Workers of Iniquity.</ns0:hi> 3. It is plain that this Man was no such Person, as <ns0:hi>Sceva's</ns0:hi> Sons of whom we Read, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14, 15, 16. for the Devils resisted<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> them, tho they also used the Name of Christ.<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> It was a time exceeding famous for some of the more <ns0:hi>Extraordinary Gifts of the Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> and it is not to be wonder<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, if some in this time for the Glory of God, received some Crums of that plentiful Benevolence, tho they were but imper<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect Disciples, yet being no Enemies. <ns0:hi>Caiphas</ns0:hi> Prophesied, <ns0:hi>Ioh</ns0:hi> 11.51.52. and tho I do think that the <ns0:hi>Children of the Phari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sees</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 12.27. as Persons that cast out Devils, is best interpreted of those sent out by Christ (the <ns0:hi>Twelve</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Seventy</ns0:hi>) yet some are of another mind. Some think this Man, tho he did not follow Christ, and his Disciples as a constant Companion, yet was one who favoured, and had received the Gospel: Or else one of <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples, and so one, who, tho he was not formally joyned with the followers of Christ, yet was a Friend of that great Bridegroom. So as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> and the rest for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bidding him, seemed to be guilty of two no small Errors. 1. <ns0:hi>En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vying for Christs sake,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> did for <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> his sake, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 11.28. as <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples did for their Masters sake, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.26. willing that Christ, and those whom he sent out should have all the Honour, of those Miraculous Operations. 2. <ns0:hi>Limiting the Grace of Christ to that Congregatton, which followed Christ, and the Twelve.</ns0:hi> A thing that good Men are to prone unto. How much better was the Spirit of <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> who tells us <ns0:hi>Philip.</ns0:hi> 1.15. that <ns0:hi>altho some Preached Christ of envy, and strife, yet he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joyced, and would rejoyce that Christ was Preached, whether in pretence, or in Truth, v.</ns0:hi> 18. Christ would have all his People of such a Spirit, as not to hinder<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but commend, not to Envy, but to rejoyce in the doing of good by any, whether they did fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low him or no. Some do think that at that time it pleased God, that for the Honour of his Son Jesus Christ, he did Concur with those, that Named his Name in such Miraculous Operations. Sure we are that Christ reproveth <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and Commandeth them not to <ns0:hi>forbid</ns0:hi> this Man, giving this for a reason, That his owning the Name of Christ, so far as to use it in such an Operation, had at least so much kindness for him, as he was no Enemy, he would not Curse him, nor speak Evil of him, which cometh up to that of the Apostle, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>No Man speaking by the Spirit of God, calleth Iesus Accursed,</ns0:hi> and no Man can say Jesus is the Lord but by the Spirit. <ns0:hi>For he that is not against us, is on our part.</ns0:hi> If a Man be not an open Enemy to Christ, he ought to be presumed to be his Friend, at leas<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> so far as not to be discouraged in doing a good Work.</ns0:note>
